requirement_text: UCLA does not accept the Common App; you will need to fill out the UC Application. To begin the application process, use the University of California's online application (UC Application).
limitations: No requirement_category_db value in the enum precisely denotes 'which application platform this institution uses'; supplemental_requirement is the closest available fit, not a semantic match. Do not read this record as describing a document supplement — it documents the application SYSTEM itself.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (brief's top risk for this pass): confirmed directly on UCLA's own official page, not assumed. UCLA participates exclusively in the University of California's own centralized 'UC Application' (apply.universityofcalifornia.edu), operated by the UC Office of the President for all 9 UC undergraduate campuses at once. UCLA does NOT accept the Common Application, Coalition App, or any other third-party platform. This is a genuinely different shape from every private university in wave 1 (MIT/Stanford/Harvard/Yale/Princeton/Columbia all use Common App or their own single-campus system) — one shared application serves all UC campuses simultaneously; a UCLA-specific field on the shared form indicates campus/major choice.

requirement_text: UCLA will not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes. If you choose to submit test scores as part of your application, they may be used as an alternative method of fulfilling minimum requirements for eligibility or for course placement after you enroll.
limitations: This is UCLA's own restatement of the systemwide UC test-blind policy, not a UCLA-specific deviation. Do not evaluate a missing SAT/ACT score as not_met for any purpose other than the narrow post-enrollment placement/eligibility-verification use named here.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (brief-flagged): verified directly, not assumed. UC-wide policy confirmed independently on the UC systemwide site: 'UC will not consider SAT or ACT test scores when making admissions decisions or awarding scholarships. They may be used as an alternative method of fulfilling minimum requirements for eligibility or for course placement after you enroll.' (admission.universityofcalifornia.edu, matches UCLA's wording almost verbatim, corroborating rather than duplicating). This is TEST-BLIND, not merely test-optional: UC's stated policy is that scores are not considered even if voluntarily submitted for admission purposes, which is a stronger exclusion than MIT/Harvard/Yale-style test-required or test-optional-with-consideration policies recorded in wave 1. Effective since UC Regents' 2020 policy action (not independently re-verified as a historical citation this pass; current live-page wording is unhedged present tense as of retrieval 2026-08-21, consistent with a stable, unreversed policy). A parallel agent researching UC Berkeley should independently confirm the identical systemwide fact from Berkeley's own page — same underlying UC Regents policy, not duplicate evidence.

requirement_text: You must complete 15 A-G courses with at least 11 courses finished prior to the beginning of your last year of high school. To be competitive in the UCLA admission process, applicants should present an academic profile much stronger than any minimum UC admission requirements.
limitations: This is the minimum eligibility floor, explicitly stated by UCLA as below the level of a competitive applicant. Do not treat 15/11 as a target; treat it as a gate below which an applicant is not UC-eligible at all.
researcher_notes: 'A-G' is California's statewide college-prep subject-requirement framework (used for UC and CSU eligibility), not a UCLA-specific invention; UCLA administers the same statewide list. 'Each application for admission is reviewed within the context of courses available to that student. If a particular required subject is not available, we'll consider your application without it' (same page) — record this as a contextual carve-out, not reflected as its own row.

requirement_text: No specific minimum GPA is stated as an admission requirement on UCLA's first-year requirements page; the page instead links to a GPA calculator and frames GPA as one input into holistic 'comprehensive review.'
limitations: Absence of a stated minimum is itself the finding — do not synthesize a threshold (e.g., from historical admit-GPA statistics) and store it as if UCLA published it as a requirement. See REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0037 for admitted-class GPA statistics, which are explicitly descriptive, not a requirement.
researcher_notes: Consistent with UC's systemwide 'comprehensive review' model (REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0013): GPA is one of ~13 factors, not a standalone gate, and the UC Statewide Eligibility Index (a separate minimum-eligibility calculation using GPA banded against test scores) was retired UC-wide alongside the test-blind policy shift — not independently re-verified this pass as a historical citation, noted only as context for why no bare numeric GPA floor is published.

requirement_text: When reviewing an application, we implement a holistic review process, which includes looking at some of the following criteria: Achievement in high school or college coursework; Personal qualities; Likely contributions to the intellectual and cultural vitality of our campus; Achievement in academic enrichment programs; Other achievements in any field of intellectual or creative endeavor, including the performing arts, athletics, community service, etc.
limitations: Explicitly non-exhaustive ('some of the following') and non-formulaic holistic criteria, not a pass/fail checklist. Do not treat any single bullet as independently gating.
researcher_notes: UCLA's own public-facing short-form (5-bullet) framing of comprehensive review. UCLA's page separately states 'there are 13 criteria that our faculty have approved for first-year admission consideration' — see REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0013 for the fuller UC systemwide 13-factor list, which this UCLA summary is consistent with (not contradictory, just abridged).

requirement_text: Some factors we may consider are: Academic grade point average in all completed A-G courses, including additional points for completed UC-certified honors courses. Number of, content of and performance in all A-G subject areas beyond the minimum requirements. Number of and performance in UC-approved honors, Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate Higher Level and transferable college courses. Identification by UC as being ranked in the top 9 percent of your high school class at the end of your junior year (Eligible in the Local Context, or ELC). Quality of your senior-year program as measured by the type and number of academic courses in any A-G subject area in progress or planned. Quality of your academic performance relative to the educational opportunities available in your high school. Outstanding performance in one or more specific subject areas. Outstanding work in one or more special projects in any academic field of study. Recent, marked improvement in academic performance as demonstrated by academic GPA and the quality of coursework completed or in progress. Special talents, achievements and awards in a particular field... Completion of special projects undertaken in the context of your high school curriculum or in conjunction with special school events, projects or programs. Academic accomplishments in light of your life experiences and special circumstances, including but not limited to: disabilities, low family income, first generation to attend college, need to work, disadvantaged social or educational environment, difficult personal and family situations or circumstances, refugee status or veteran status. Location of your secondary school and residence.
limitations: One long bullet (special talents/achievements/awards) was trimmed with '...' for length in this record; full clause is 'Special talents, achievements and awards in a particular field, such as visual and performing arts, communication or athletic endeavors; special skills, such as demonstrated written and oral proficiency in other languages; special interests, such as intensive study and exploration of other cultures; experiences that demonstrate unusual promise for leadership, such as significant community service or significant participation in student government; or other significant experiences or achievements that demonstrate the student's promise for contributing to the intellectual vitality of a campus.' Marked extracted_summary rather than verbatim_quoted because of that trim, even though every included word is copied exactly. Holistic factors, non-formulaic, none independently gating; 'The UC undergraduate admission process does not discriminate against, or provide preferential treatment to, any individual on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin, consistent with federal and state law' (same page, not separately recorded as a requirement row).
researcher_notes: This is the UC Regents-approved, systemwide 'comprehensive review' factor list — counted, it is 13 numbered items, matching UCLA's own page's claim of '13 criteria that our faculty have approved.' Applies identically to all 9 UC undergraduate campuses; page states 'While all UC campuses use the same factors to evaluate applications, they often apply these factors differently' and links to a UCLA-specific selection-process page not separately fetched this pass. A UC Berkeley research agent citing the identical list from Berkeley's own page would be good corroboration, not duplication — same underlying systemwide policy document.

requirement_text: You will have 8 questions to choose from. You must respond to only 4 of the 8 questions. Each response is limited to a maximum of 350 words. 1. Describe an example of your leadership experience... 2. Every person has a creative side... describe how you express your creative side. 3. What would you say is your greatest talent or skill?... 4. Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced. 5. Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge... 6. Think about an academic subject that inspires you... 7. What have you done to make your school or your community a better place? 8. Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
limitations: Question prompts 1-3 and 5-6 were trimmed with '...' for length; the full text of all 8 prompts plus per-question guidance ('Things to consider') is on the source page. Marked extracted_summary due to the trims even though retained text is copied exactly. 'All questions are equal... there is no advantage or disadvantage to choosing certain questions over others.'
researcher_notes: UC-systemwide, applies identically to UCLA. UCLA's own personal-insight-questions page (admission.ucla.edu/apply/personal-insight-questions) gives writing tips but explicitly defers the actual question text to this UC systemwide page ('Please visit the University of California site for more help with your personal insight questions, including the text of the questions'), confirmed by direct fetch of both pages. Also includes an unscored freeform 'additional comments' field per the UC page: 'Use the additional comments field if there are issues you'd like to address... This shouldn't be an essay, but rather a place to note unusual circumstances.'

requirement_text: If you've completed all your secondary school/high school in a country where English is not the language of instruction, you can demonstrate proficiency by taking one of these exams no later than December of your final year of high school/secondary school and earning the required scores. [UCLA framing:] If all of your high school/secondary school education was completed in English, you are considered proficient and do not need to satisfy this requirement. However, if you've completed all or some high school or secondary school in a country where English was not the language of instruction, you will be required to demonstrate English proficiency if you have had less than 3 years of instruction in English.
limitations: This is the TRIGGER condition (who must test), not the score threshold itself — see REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0016 through UCL0020 for UCLA's specific score thresholds. The bracketed UCLA-specific sentence and the unbracketed UC systemwide sentence are combined here as one requirement_text because they state the identical eligibility trigger in near-identical language across the two official pages; source_url points to UCLA's own page as primary.
researcher_notes: Corroborated near-verbatim between admission.ucla.edu/apply/international-applicants and admission.universityofcalifornia.edu's english-language-proficiency page — same rule, two independent official pages, not a conflict.

requirement_text: We look for competitive English proficiency scores, including a TOEFL iBT score of 5 or higher (with sub-scores of 5 or higher) on the revised scale (effective January 21, 2026)...
limitations: Phrased as what UCLA 'looks for' ('competitive... scores'), not explicitly as a hard pass/fail minimum — softer framing than a stated cutoff, but this is the only numeric figure UCLA itself publishes, and it is materially higher than the UC systemwide eligibility floor (TOEFL iBT 4.5 on this same new scale — see REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0020). Do not silently substitute the systemwide floor for this UCLA-specific figure.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: '5 or higher (with sub-scores of 5 or higher)' is stated entirely on ETS's new 1-6 scale (effective 2026-01-21, per scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md's ETS findings), including the per-section (sub-score) figure. Unlike the University of Glasgow defect documented in that file (a post-cutover per-subtest minimum stated on the discontinued 0-30 legacy subtest scale, which ETS no longer reports and is therefore unsatisfiable), UCLA's sub-score requirement here is stated ON the new 1-6 scale that ETS actually reports post-cutover for section scores — fully satisfiable as published, no partial-unsatisfiability defect found.

requirement_text: ...or above 100 (with sub-scores above 24) on the previous 120-point scale, as well as 7.5 or above on the IELTS or 135 or higher on the Duolingo English Test (DET). [TOEFL clause only extracted here; IELTS/DET recorded separately.]
limitations: Applies to TOEFL iBT tests taken before the 2026-01-21 cutover. Framed as a 'competitive' expectation, not an explicit hard minimum. Materially higher than the UC systemwide floor of 80 on the same legacy scale (REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0020).
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: bound explicitly to 'the previous 120-point scale' — i.e., pre-2026-01-21 legacy TOEFL iBT, both the overall (100) and per-section sub-score (24, on the legacy 0-30 subtest scale) figures are internally scale-consistent (both legacy), so this row does not exhibit the Glasgow-style partial-unsatisfiability defect: a legacy-scale test report legitimately carries legacy-scale subtest scores.

requirement_text: 7.5 or above on the IELTS
limitations: Framed as a 'competitive' expectation on UCLA's page, not explicitly an absolute cutoff. Higher than the UC systemwide floor of 6.5 (REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0020).
researcher_notes: IELTS scale is unaffected by the January 2026 TOEFL rescale (confirmed unaffected in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md's audit).

requirement_text: 135 or higher on the Duolingo English Test (DET)
limitations: Framed as a 'competitive' expectation, not explicitly an absolute cutoff. Higher than the UC systemwide floor of 115 (REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0020).
researcher_notes: Duolingo English Test scale (10-160) has no scale-versioning issue analogous to TOEFL's; no test_scale enum value is offered for DET in this schema (options are TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge/SAT-specific or null) — left null rather than forcing a mismatched enum value.

requirement_text: You can demonstrate proficiency by meeting any of the following exam benchmarks... Score 3, 4 or 5 on the AP examination in English Language and Composition, or English Literature and Composition. Score 6 or 7 on the IB Standard Level examination in English (Language A only). Score 5, 6 or 7 on the IB Higher Level examination in English (Language A only). Score 6.5 or higher on the International English Language Testing System (IELTS)*. TOEFL: iBT or iBT Home Edition: Effective January 2026 a minimum score of 4.5 or better. Prior to January 2026 a minimum score of 80 or better. Duolingo English Test (DET): Minimum score of 115. Score of 24 or higher on the ACT English Language Arts (ELA). Score of 31 or higher on the SAT Writing and Language. Earn a grade of C or better in a UC-transferable college course in English composition (worth 3 semester or 4-5 quarter units).
limitations: This is the UC SYSTEMWIDE MINIMUM eligibility floor, explicitly lower than UCLA's own stated 'competitive' expectations (REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0016 through UCL0019). Page states: 'A UC campus may require a score higher than the minimum for admission selection' — UCLA does so. Do not evaluate a UCLA applicant against this floor alone; it establishes eligibility, not competitiveness. The AP/IB/ACT/SAT/course-grade alternative pathways are NOT mentioned anywhere on UCLA's own international-applicants page and would be missed by an evaluator relying only on UCLA's page.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK, systemwide floor: TOEFL clause explicitly gives both eras ('Effective January 2026... 4.5... Prior to January 2026... 80'), each internally consistent and each an OVERALL-only figure (no per-section minimum stated at this systemwide-floor level, unlike UCLA's own higher bar which does add sub-score minimums) — no partial-unsatisfiability defect at the systemwide-floor level.

requirement_text: Please note: UC does not accept IELTS One Skill Retake or MyBest TOEFL; only the highest composite score from a single sitting is allowed. Also, the digital SAT Reading and Writing section score has not been approved to meet English language proficiency.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION TRAP (matches trap #3 in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md exactly): a numerically-qualifying IELTS One Skill Retake or MyBest TOEFL composite is still rejected on provenance — 'only the highest composite score from a single sitting is allowed.' A threshold comparison alone cannot distinguish a superscored/retake composite from a single-sitting one with the identical number; per that finding's recommended interim behavior, any stored student TOEFL/IELTS score lacking a provenance flag (single-sitting vs. superscore vs. retake) should evaluate to needs_manual_review against REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0016/17/18, not a confident met.

requirement_text: UCLA does not award scholarships or financial aid to undergraduate students who are not citizens or permanent residents of the United States.
limitations: A hard institutional-aid exclusion by citizenship/residency status, not an admission-eligibility rule — international students remain admissible; they are simply ineligible for UCLA/UC-administered aid. Private scholarships remain available and are unaffected by this exclusion.
researcher_notes: Sharpens the FAFSA/Dream Act distinction recorded at REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0032: both of those programs require US citizenship, permanent residency, or AB 540 eligibility; a genuinely non-resident international applicant qualifies for neither, and per this record also receives no UCLA institutional aid as a backstop.

researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (brief-flagged): directly confirms both parts of the brief's prediction — (1) no ED/EA/REA distinction of any kind exists at UCLA, only the single Oct 1 - Nov 30 filing period (see DL-2026-08-21-UCL0001); do not force-fit an 'early round' record. (2) UCLA explicitly does NOT participate in the UC systemwide 'Spring [entry] application filing period for select campuses' that the UC systemwide dates-and-deadlines page separately advertises (July 1-31, for spring-admitting campuses) — see DL-2026-08-21-UCL0028 for that systemwide fact, recorded specifically so it is not mistakenly attributed to UCLA. requirement_category_db enum has no 'admission round structure' value; application_deadline was chosen as the closest fit since the substance of this fact is about the shape of the deadline structure itself.

requirement_text: If you are a citizen or eligible non-citizen, and meet the requirements for an AB 540 nonresident tuition exemption, you may qualify for state aid, in addition to federal and UC aid. Follow the steps above, except instead of filing a California Dream Act Application, file a Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). [Undocumented students:] As an undocumented student, you may be eligible for state and UC aid, as well as private scholarships. Undocumented students are ineligible for federal aid (including federal loans and grants, and the federal work-study program), but now have the option to borrow student loans through the DREAM Loan Program.
scope: California AB 540-eligible students and California residents; not applicable to international (non-resident-alien) applicants, who are covered separately by REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0022.
limitations: requirement_category_db has no dedicated financial-aid-eligibility value; supplemental_requirement used as closest fit. This describes AID eligibility, not admission eligibility — an applicant ineligible for aid under this rule remains fully admissible.
researcher_notes: RESIDENCY-BASED AID-ELIGIBILITY DISTINCTION (brief-requested): the operative fork is citizenship/immigration status, not simple domestic-vs-international — (a) US citizens & eligible non-citizens file FAFSA; (b) undocumented students who qualify for the AB 540 nonresident tuition exemption file the California Dream Act Application instead and may still get state + UC aid, just not federal aid; (c) undocumented students who do NOT qualify for AB 540 get no federal, state, or institutional aid at all (see REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0033); (d) international (non-resident-alien, non-AB540) students get no UCLA institutional aid at all (REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0022) and are not eligible to file either FAFSA or the Dream Act application. DACA status does not itself confer AB 540 eligibility or ineligibility — see REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0034.

requirement_text: If you're an undocumented student and are not eligible for an AB 540 nonresident tuition exemption, you will be ineligible for all federal, state and institutional aid. Private loans and scholarships are the only financial aid options.
scope: Undocumented students who do not qualify for the AB 540 nonresident tuition exemption.
researcher_notes: Sharpest edge of the residency-based aid framework recorded at REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0032 — the one population with zero federal/state/institutional aid pathway at all, admission eligibility notwithstanding.

requirement_text: If you have DACA status, you should not fill out a FAFSA, even if you have a Social Security number. If you're anticipating being eligible for AB 540, you should still fill out the Cal Dream Act application. DACA has no effect on eligibility for the AB 540 nonresident tuition exemption or financial aid.
researcher_notes: NAMED-EXCLUSION-STYLE TRAP: a DACA recipient possessing a valid SSN could easily be assumed FAFSA-eligible by SSN possession alone; the source explicitly instructs the opposite ('should not fill out a FAFSA, even if you have a Social Security number'). An eligibility evaluator keyed only on 'has SSN' would produce a confidently wrong answer here.

requirement_text: Filing period expected to be available on or before October 1 for Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and Dream Act Application for all applicants; filing period opens for GPA Verification Form (required for California residents only for Cal Grant consideration)
scope: GPA Verification Form specifically applies to California residents only, per the source's own parenthetical; the FAFSA/Dream Act filing-period opening applies to all applicants.
limitations: requirement_category_db has no dedicated 'aid form eligibility scope' value; application_deadline used as closest fit since the clause is calendar-shaped. The GPA Verification Form's substantive purpose (Cal Grant eligibility, California residents only) is the residency-scoped fact; the corresponding date is recorded separately in the deadlines file (DL-2026-08-21-UCL0004).
researcher_notes: Directly answers the brief's ask to record residency-based aid-eligibility distinctions: Cal Grant GPA verification is explicitly California-resident-only, unlike FAFSA/Dream Act Application filing-period opening, which is university-wide ('for all applicants').

requirement_text: Overview by School Applied To (Fall 2025): Total 145,085 applicants, 13,659 admits, 9.4% admit rate. The College: 98,459 applicants, 11% admit rate. Samueli School of Engineering: 33,052 applicants, 6.8% admit rate. School of Theater, Film & Television: 3,293 applicants, 4.3% admit rate. School of the Arts & Architecture: 3,437 applicants, 5.1% admit rate. Herb Alpert School of Music: 1,175 applicants, 24% admit rate. School of Nursing: 5,669 applicants, 0.5% admit rate.
limitations: HISTORICAL, DESCRIPTIVE INSTITUTIONAL STATISTIC, NOT AN ADMISSION REQUIREMENT AND NOT AN INDIVIDUAL PROBABILITY. Fall 2025 is two cycles stale relative to this batch's Fall 2027 research target; UCLA had not published a more recent first-year profile page as of retrieval (2026-08-21) — treat the Fall 2027 (or even Fall 2026) equivalent as CURRENT_CYCLE_NOT_PUBLISHED. Per ORYN's own non-negotiable product requirements, a general institutional/school acceptance rate must never be presented as, or used to compute, an individual student's probability of admission.
researcher_notes: Directly responsive to the brief's flag that 'UCLA has notably different admission emphases across its colleges/schools': admit rates by school-applied-to range from 0.5% (Nursing) to 24% (Herb Alpert School of Music) against a 9.4% campus-wide rate — an order-of-magnitude spread. Note this contradicts a third-party admissions-consulting site's claim (crimsoneducation.org, not used as a source per this lane's evidence rules) of a flat '12%' UCLA admit rate — official data shows 9.4% campus-wide for the most recent published cycle, illustrating exactly why third-party aggregator numbers are excluded from this corpus.

requirement_text: GPA statistics for admitted first-year students, Fall 2025: Weighted GPA — Median 4.61, Middle 25%-75% 4.44-4.78. Unweighted GPA — Median 4.00, Middle 25%-75% 3.95-4.00. All GPAs are calculated from courses completed in grades 10 and 11. The fully weighted GPA includes an extra grade point for all UC-approved honors courses... in which a grade of C or higher is earned. The maximum value possible is 5.00. The unweighted GPA does not include any extra grade points for honors courses. The maximum value possible is 4.00.
limitations: DESCRIPTIVE STATISTIC OF ADMITTED STUDENTS, NOT A MINIMUM REQUIREMENT — category/db forced into 'minimum_grade' for schema-fit only; see REQ-2026-08-21-UCL0011, which explicitly confirms UCLA publishes no stated minimum GPA. Fall 2025 is two cycles stale relative to Fall 2027. Do not evaluate a student's GPA against this median/IQR as a pass/fail gate; at most it is descriptive context for academic-fit scoring, clearly labeled as historical and non-binding.
researcher_notes: Corroborates, with more precision, the '4.0 average unweighted GPA for Fall 2025 admits' one-line figure separately given on admission.ucla.edu/apply/first-year (not recorded as its own row to avoid duplication — same underlying fact, this record is the fuller source).
